title: Mirror Speculative Decoding: Breaking the Serial Barrier in LLM Inference
quote: Target models are distributed across eight M2 Ultra GPUs using Megatron-style tensor parallelism
proves: Apple work maps draft to NPUs and target verification to GPUs (8 M2 Ultra GPUs TP + 8 NPUs); claims 2.8x-5.8x wall-time speedup on SpecBench for 14B-66B targets, 30% over EAGLE3; cross-device token exchanges called microsecond-scale
does_not_prove: Server-scale multi-chip rig, not a single laptop SoC; no measured interconnect numbers; does not study contention on shared memory bandwidth when NPU and GPU share DRAM, nor power/thermal
bearing: Prior art for NPU-draft/GPU-verify; threatens any 'draft on NPU' novelty claim

title: DuoDecoding: Hardware-aware Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding with Dynamic Multi-Sequence Drafting
quote: strategically deploys the draft and target models on the CPU and GPU respectively
proves: Draft on CPU, target on GPU; up to 2.61x latency speedup and TTFT 83% of conventional SD
does_not_prove: Batch-1 single-user focus; no serving load, no unified-memory SoC
bearing: Prior art for CPU-draft placement; weakens CPU-drafter candidates

title: Dovetail: A CPU/GPU Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding for LLM inference
quote: Dovetail deploys a draft model on the GPU to perform preliminary predictions
proves: Reverse split: draft on GPU, target verify on CPU; 1.79x-10.1x speedups on 13B models across devices
does_not_prove: Consumer single-user setting; abstract gives no GPU memory numbers; does not cover datacenter serving
bearing: Prior art for GPU-draft/CPU-target in memory-poor regime

title: Sequoia: Scalable, Robust, and Hardware-aware Speculative Decoding
quote: Sequoia selects much larger trees in the offloading setting (768 tokens) than in the on-device setting (64 to 128 tokens)
proves: Hardware-aware optimizer measures t(n) empirically per model and hardware and picks tree size/depth; offloaded Llama2-70B on L40 at 0.56 s/token (9.96x over own offloading baseline); up to 4.04x on A100
does_not_prove: t(n) is profiled once offline; does not track t(n) changes at runtime (power caps, co-tenancy, thermal throttling, batch changes)
bearing: Threatens 'hardware-aware tree/K tuning' as novel; leaves runtime-drifting t(n) open

title: SMART: When is it Actually Worth Expanding a Speculative Tree?
quote: This often leads to negative wall-clock speedup when batch sizes increase or hardware saturation limits are reached.
proves: Tree drafting/verification overhead can grow super-linearly; marginal-analysis tree expansion gives +15.4% (LLM) and +20.0% (MLLM) in compute-bound batching across diverse GPU architectures
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no per-GPU breakdown; offline vs online calibration unclear
bearing: Threatens per-accelerator tree-size candidates (crowded area)

title: Trajectory-Level Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

does_not_prove: Hardware proposal (evaluation platform not stated in abstract, likely simulated); not buildable on commodity hardware

title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling
quote: augments traditional DVFS processor frequency tuning with two additional workload-specific knobs
proves: Joint DVFS + speculative decoding + variable verification depth on device: up to 23.1% speedup and 52.4% energy reduction
does_not_prove: Abstract does not name device or say which unit is scaled in draft vs verify phases; single-request on-device

title: Accelerating Mobile Language Model via Speculative Decoding and NPU-Coordinated Execution

title: SpecOffload: Unlocking Latent GPU Capacity for LLM Inference on Resource-Constrained Devices
quote: improves GPU core utilization by 4.49x and boosts inference throughput by 2.54x
proves: In offloading regimes, idle GPU can store and run a draft model; 2.54x throughput over best baseline
does_not_prove: Throughput-oriented offline batch; GPU model not named in abstract

title: ShadowSpec: Towards Zero Speculation Overhead for Substitute Speculative Decoding

proves: Overlapping draft tree extension with target parameter loading over PCIe gives 17-54% over SubSpec on a consumer GPU
does_not_prove: Workshop poster; GPU not named; single-user offloading only
bearing: Offloading overlap already done (latest in that line)

title: Cross-Family Speculative Decoding for Polish Language Models on Apple Silicon: An Empirical Evaluation of Bielik 11B with UAG-Extended MLX-LM
quote: verification cost on unified memory does not amortize as theory predicts

title: Enabling Speculative Speculative Decoding on MI300X

title: LP-Spec: Leveraging LPDDR PIM for Efficient LLM Mobile Speculative Inference with Architecture-Dataflow Co-Optimization
quote: speculative inference results in more compute-intensive GEMM operations

does_not_prove: Architecture proposal; simulation status not stated in abstract

title: SPECTRA: Adaptive Execution of Speculative Decoding on a Runtime-Reconfigurable Tiled Architecture
quote: Within each tile, the compute engine switches between systolic execution for GEMMs and vector-lane execution for GEMVs
proves: Verification is an intermediate regime between decode and prefill; per-kernel reconfiguration on a 20-tile FPGA prototype gives up to 2.09x plus 1.25x
does_not_prove: Small models (Pythia, SmolLM2, GPT-2); custom hardware
bearing: Supports verify-as-distinct-regime; hardware angle taken

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding

title: TensorRT-Edge-LLM Performance Benchmarks (0.7.0)
quote: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct INT4 AWQ INT4 AWQ 8 2735.5 3056 118.0 5.21 0.87x
proves: On Jetson AGX Thor (Blackwell SM110), EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B: NVFP4 1 -> 3.45x, batch 8 -> 1.57x; INT4 AWQ batch 1 -> 1.59x, batch 8 -> 0.87x (slower) at same acceptance ~5.2

does_not_prove: Single 2xA800 PCIe setup, two model pairs; no green contexts; contention controlled heuristically

title: HeteroReason: Heterogeneous FPGA-GPU Acceleration for Disaggregated Speculative Reasoning
quote: the draft model is offloaded to the FPGA

does_not_prove: Reasoning-step speculation, not token-level; hardware unnamed in abstract

title: StarSD: One-for-Many Speculative Decoding

title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
quote: speculative decoding pays off only when verification is genuinely batch-parallel and the draft/target latency gap is real

does_not_prove: Single-request workload; mechanism not explained on page; machines unnamed
bearing: Strong negative for laptop speculation; opportunity may be to explain why (verify kernel shape)
